caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 147 of 1992
lawyer:
Santiranjan Karmaker, Advocate-on-Record, Supreme Court — For the Petitioner. 
Not represented — Respondents.
parties:
Muzaffar Ali Bepari ----- Preemptee-Petitioner
vs.
Omar Ali & ors ----- Pre-emptor-Respondents.
full_judgment:
Muhammad Abdur Rouf J : The Pre-emptee-Petitioner has sought for leave to appeal from the judgment of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 155 of 1987 passed on 26 January 1992 discharging the Rule and thereby upholding the judgment and order of the Subordinate Judge, passed on 24 January 1987 allowing Miscellaneous Appeal No. 108 of 1985 whereby the preemption case instituted under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act was allowed after setting aside the judgment and order passed by the Munsif, Gaforgaon on 30th April, 1985 dismissing Pre-emption Case No. 75 of 1984. 

 2. Respondent Nos. 2 and 3 on 6.12.77 sold the land in question for Take 8,000.00 to the petitioner and the sale deed was registered under section 60 of the Registration Act on 30.1.79. Respondent No. 1 on 30.5.79 filed the case seeking pre-emption of the said land claiming himself as a co-sharer by purchase as well as by inheritance in respect of the relevant tenancy and terming the petitioner as a stranger purchaser. The petitioner contested the case by filing a written objection and denying that respondent No. 1 is a co-sharer of the holding in question. His case is that he had to re-transfer the case land of respondent Nos. 2 and 3 on 24.1.78 in pursuance of an agreement and, as such, the right of pre-emption did not exist when the case was filed. Two PWs and three OPWs were examined in the case. Deed of reconveyance Ext. 4 dated 24.1.78 and two other kabalas of the same date namely, Exts. 5 and 5(a) by which respondent Nos. 2 and 3 once again sold the said land to the sons and wife of the petitioner have been marked on the side of the Pre-emptor. The trial Court dismissed the case holding that on the date of filing the case the right of pre-emption did not exist as the land had reverted back to the sellers on 24.1.78. Upon an appeal taken by the pre-emptor the appellate Court reversed the judgment of the trial Court and allowed the pre-emption holding, inter alia, that the transaction alleged to have been affected vide Exts. 4 and 5 series being sham transactions did not affect the right of preemption of the Pre-emptor. A Single Bench of the High Court Division by the impugned judgment has maintained the judgment and order of the lower appellate Court.
